Known science foundations of Orbital Habitat Foundry.

The ISS demonstrates long-duration habitation. Bigelow's BEAM inflatable module has operated on the ISS since 2016. O'Neill's Island Three studies detailed kilometer-scale rotating habitats. Asteroid-material processing has only lab-scale demonstrations. No orbital factory has produced habitat structures from space resources.

Key quantity check (ISS pressurized volume in cubic meters / O'Neill Island Three design volume): computed ratio 9.16e-08 against the reference value, relative error 0, within the stated tolerance of 0.5. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

Physical and engineering constraints on Orbital Habitat Foundry.

Processing asteroid material into structural feedstock is unproven at scale. Megastructure assembly needs robotics far beyond current capability. Radiation shielding mass dominates habitat design.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 10 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is Island Three design mass vs asteroid material processed in space at 10 orders of magnitude (Island Three design mass larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.
